Author: @undeadpm4208
Content:
Credit to Bleached0 in the comments (replied to mw2zorzest) who pointed out: “the painting in the closet is the painting of Saturn devouring his son, which is basically the Roman version of the story of the Titans and how Cronus eats Zeus and his siblings”

​​⁠​⁠​⁠​⁠The artist who created that rendition of Satern Devouring His Son was done by an artist named Francisco Goya, part of his series known as Black Paintings (as told to me from art history videos) that wasn’t meant to be seen by the public, but for himself. Goya shows the dark side of humanity in his paintings, where here, the myth of Satern Devouring His Son due is due to a prophecy that Satern will be slaughtered by his son, is portrayed by a father driven by paranoia, fear, and desperation that leads him to the monstrous action of eating his son. Very fitting for the game. Goya is one of my favorite artists. If you don’t mind peering into the abyss, then I highly recommend his work.

Content: The Painting at 14:22 appears to be a recreation of Spanish Artist Francisco Goya's; "Saturn Devouring His Son", one of his most horrific and iconic paintings. Saturn Devouring his sun was a tale of how the Greek God Saturn lived in fear of a prophecy, one that said his Children would overthrow him. In a crazed frenzy to prevent this, his fear culminated in consuming his offspring. The painting here appears to show a rat instead of Saturn and based on the rats jumping down from the vents into the baby's crib, we can infer that rat consumed this man's son, ergo, his vengeful vendetta against rats.

Best wishes,

Author: @kloogsisconfident4633
Content:
So "Abandon all hope, ye who enter here" is actually a quote from Dante's poem "Canto III" under the section "Inferno". It was originally translated from the italian, "Lasciate ogne speranza, voi ch'intrate" and is supposedly what is written above the gates of hell before Dante enters hell for the first time with his guide Virgil from purgatory. So here is my theory on the games story:

You start in an empty cornfield (purgatory) and as you come to terms with where you are your house appears. As you enter it you are literally entering hell. Why are you in hell? Well because you are a serial killer. You are being punished for your crimes. There are multiple missed bits of information that lead me to this conclusion. 1) the quote "did she know what was happening under the floorboards" 2) on the TVs throughout the game you can see different people all in the same pose (tied up and kneeling on the ground). This perhaps is your characters "trophies". A VHS tape of the victims. 3) there are barrels everywhere, which leads me to believe that your MO was to stuff them in a barrel in some way (Maybe dahmer style). 

I believe that the bodies in the basement led to a rat infestation. The rat infestation got so bad to where they climbed through the vents and ate your child alive while they were sleeping. Your wife through her grief and anger found out about what you were and so you had no choice but to kill her or have your secret be uncovered. My guess is you strangled her (hence why you strangle the rat). Everything is a punishment. Holding and shaking the rat is a punishment for your childs tragic death. Strangling the rat is a reminder of what you did to your wife. You spend forever in a maze that is your own house reliving over and over again your actions and the crimes you committed in hell. The quote "i wonder if a fall from this height would kill me" is most likely a reference to how the killer died. My best guess is he knew the cops would come for him (hence the red and blue lights at the end) as his wife suddenly disappeared and he decided to take his own life beginning the events of the game. Your rat friend is actually your guide, your virgil, guiding you through why you are in hell.

However, the truest hell is spending an eternity with nothing but rat puns.

How the design meeting went:
"Ratshaker... that's an interesting name for a game. What's it about?"

"You shake a rat."

"...Right, we got that already. But how? Is there some new, innovative game mechanic?"

"Nope. They just shake the mouse."

"Okay, it feels like we aren't getting anywhere... can you tell us more about other parts of the game?"

"You also squeeze the rat."

"Wha... squeeze?"

"Yeah. To choke it."

"This... doesn't seem very..."

"So you can open doors."

"Sorry, what?"

"You choke the rat to open doors. And turn on lights. And, pretty much do any kind of interaction with the world around you."

*Stares in horror*

"Oh, but you have to make sure you shake the rat enough first. You know, to charge your choke-grip."

"This doesn't sound like a very kid-friendly game..."

"Oh, thanks for reminding me! So the lore is..."

Author: @yourfavoritejewishmom
Content:
I really was expecting this to be about having shaken the baby. Voice from beyond at the beginning insisting that shaking “the rat” will fix everything and make it stop reminded me of what leads new parents to shake babies in the first place, crippling exhaustion mixed with frustration, desperation, etc. Your brain breaks and goes “please, make it stop!” And unfortunately, it does. Permanently.
My guess is, instead, our player character was a serial killer. Hence the line asking “if she knew what was going on beneath her floorboards” and all of the barrels in the basement. This led to a rat infestation the wife was trying to treat with the Rat Shaker rat poison we keep seeing ads for and boxes of. She eventually checked into the basement, and our player character snapped and killed her.
I’m unsure when the baby died, if it’s before or after dad killed mum. Regardless, rat infestations are known to be deadly to infants—if the rats aren’t entirely metaphorical of mom to begin with. That’s possible too. Ultimately I think the baby is an unnecessary addition in this story and is sort of just a cliche of the PT style genre.

Content: Here's what I think is happening. The ending makes it clear that the rats symbolize our character's wife. Which means that the scene where the rats attack the crib are symbolic of the wife mistreating the baby in some way. That ties in with the art works that all feature a parent and their dead child (e.g. the Virgin Mary with dead Jesus). When the rat says "I wonder if a fall from this height would kill me" they are referencing the wife dropping the baby, and killing it. The photo of the wife implies that she was having some sort of mental health crisis and was maybe not to blame for what happened. Our character responds to the death of the child by going berserk, and killing her. And the game is about him/us confronting this. Or perhaps just being haunted by her ghost.
